images.description: Ichthyosaurus anningae is an early Jurassic marine reptile named after pioneering paleontologist Mary Anning. This species represents one of the most successful groups of ichthyosaurs, featuring the characteristic dolphin-like body shape, four paddle-like flippers, and a powerful tail for hunting fish and squid in shallow seas.

images.title: Jianghanichthys hubeiensis
images.description: Jianghanichthys hubeiensis is an early actinopterygian fish from the Middle Triassic period of China. This primitive ray-finned fish represents an important step in the evolution of modern fish lineages.

images.title: Dickinsonia costata
images.description: Dickinsonia costata is an extinct disc-shaped organism from the Ediacaran period, characterized by its oval body and distinctive radial ribbed or ridged surface pattern. It represents one of the earliest known complex life forms and is thought to be an early member of the enigmatic Ediacaran fauna.

images.title: Platybelodon grangeri
images.description: Platybelodon grangeri was a large proboscidean from the Miocene epoch, characterized by its distinctive flattened, shovel-like lower tusks that it likely used for feeding on aquatic vegetation. This relative of modern elephants inhabited semi-arid and wetland environments across Asia and Africa.

images.title: Gomphotherium angustidens
images.description: Gomphotherium angustidens was a Miocene proboscidean characterized by its distinctive double-tusked lower jaw and grinding teeth adapted for browsing vegetation. This unusual elephant relative represents an extinct lineage that diverged from the main trunk of proboscidean evolution.

images.title: Varanosaurus acutirostris
images.description: Varanosaurus acutirostris was a small carnivorous pelycosaur from the Early Permian period, characterized by its sharp snout and predatory adaptations. This early synapsid represents an intermediate stage in the evolutionary lineage leading toward more advanced mammal-like reptiles.

images.title: Ophiacodon mirus
images.description: Ophiacodon mirus was a large pelycosaur from the early Permian period, characterized by its robust build and prominent teeth adapted for hunting. As one of the apex predators of its time, it represents an important lineage in the evolution toward modern mammals.

images.title: Metaspriggina walcotti
images.description: Metaspriggina walcotti is an early chordate from the Middle Cambrian Burgess Shale that possessed a notochord, gill bars, and fins, representing a crucial evolutionary link between invertebrates and vertebrates. This small, filter-feeding organism exemplifies the anatomical innovations that would eventually lead to the evolution of fish and all subsequent vertebrate life.

images.title: Kryptodrakon progenitor
images.description: Kryptodrakon progenitor is an early pterosaur from the Middle Jurassic period, representing one of the most basal known members of Pterosauria. This small, relatively primitive flying reptile provides important insights into pterosaur evolution and the origins of powered flight in this remarkable group.

images.title: Haootia quadriformis
images.description: Haootia quadriformis is an early cnidarian from the Ediacaran period, representing one of the oldest known jellyfish-like organisms. This small creature exhibits a four-lobed symmetry and is significant for understanding the early evolution of this diverse marine phylum.

images.title: 2014 in Paleontology
images.description: A composite paleoart illustration showcasing significant paleontological discoveries and notable extinct organisms from 2014. This poster-style artwork represents the diversity of life forms studied by paleontologists during that year.

images.title: Aquilops americanus
images.description: Aquilops americanus is one of the smallest known ceratopsians, a bipedal herbivorous dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North America. This early member of the horned dinosaur family possessed distinctive brow horns and a small frill, representing an evolutionary stage between basal ceratopsians and the larger, more elaborate forms that would dominate the Late Cretaceous.

images.title: Sauropleura pectinata
images.description: Sauropleura pectinata was a small lepospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its elongated body and reduced limbs adapted for aquatic or semi-aquatic life. This primitive tetrapod represents an early lineage of vertebrates that diverged from the main amniote radiation.

images.title: Tuditanus punctulatus
images.description: Tuditanus punctulatus was a small lepospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its slender body and primitive amniote-like features. This early tetrapod represents an important branch in early vertebrate evolution during the late Paleozoic era.

images.title: Brachydectes newberryi
images.description: Brachydectes newberryi is an early amniote from the Carboniferous period, belonging to the lepospondyls, a group of small lizard-like tetrapods with distinctive vertebral structures. This creature represents an important lineage in early tetrapod evolution before the rise of larger amniotes.

images.title: Phlegethontia longissima
images.description: Phlegethontia longissima was an elongated lepospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its extremely long, slender body and reduced limbs adapted for burrowing or aquatic locomotion. This small creature represents an early experiment in vertebrate body plans during the early evolution of amniotes.

images.title: Adelospondylus watsoni
images.description: Adelospondylus watsoni was a small, early amniote-like lepospondyl from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its elongated body and primitive vertebral structure. This early tetrapod represents an important lineage in understanding the evolution of vertebrate body plans during the Paleozoic Era.

images.title: Nanuqsaurus hoglundi
images.description: Nanuqsaurus hoglundi was a small tyrannosaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous of Alaska, notable for being one of the northernmost tyranosaurs and adapted to polar environments. This diminutive predator represents an interesting adaptation of the tyrannosaur lineage to high-latitude habitats.

images.title: Shenshou lui
images.description: Shenshou lui was an early mammal from the Middle Jurassic period of China, characterized by its small size and primitive features that provide insights into mammalian evolution during the age of dinosaurs. This genus represents an important transitional form in understanding how early mammals adapted and diversified alongside dominant reptilian fauna.

images.title: Peltephilus ferox
images.description: Peltephilus ferox was a glyptodont, an armored mammal from the Xenarthra group that lived during the Miocene to Pliocene epochs. This heavily built creature possessed a distinctive dome-shaped carapace and was one of the larger members of its family, adapted for a herbivorous lifestyle in South American grasslands and savannas.

images.title: Moeritherium lyonsi
images.description: Moeritherium lyonsi was an early proboscidean from the Eocene epoch, representing a primitive ancestor of modern elephants. This small, semi-aquatic mammal possessed a flexible trunk and tusks, and inhabited the wetlands and river systems of North Africa.

images.title: Eurotamandua joresi
images.description: Eurotamandua joresi is an extinct mammal from the Eocene epoch that represents an early relative of modern anteaters and sloths. This small, specialized insectivore possessed adaptations for feeding on ants and termites, including an elongated snout and powerful claws.

images.title: Pederpes finneyae
images.description: Pederpes finneyae is an early tetrapod from the Scottish Carboniferous period, representing one of the most primitive known limbed vertebrates with relatively well-developed digits. This small creature bridges the evolutionary gap between fish-like ancestors and more derived tetrapods, showcasing the transition from aquatic to terrestrial life.

images.title: Kulindadromeus zabaikalicus
images.description: Kulindadromeus zabaikalicus is an early ornithopod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Russia, notable for being one of the few ornithischians known to have possessed feather-like structures covering its body. This small, bipedal herbivore provides important evidence for the widespread distribution of feathered dinosaurs beyond theropods.

images.title: Eocasea martini
images.description: Eocasea martini is an early pelycosaur from the Carboniferous period, representing one of the earliest synapsids and a distant ancestor to modern mammals. This small, lizard-like creature was among the first amniotes to evolve and played an important role in early terrestrial ecosystems.

images.title: Dreadnoughtus schrani
images.description: Dreadnoughtus schrani was one of the largest land animals ever to exist, a colossal titanosaur sauropod that weighed approximately 77 metric tons and measured over 26 meters in length. This Late Cretaceous herbivore possessed a remarkably long tail that made up nearly half its body length, likely used for balance and social signaling.

images.title: Vintana sertichi
images.description: Vintana sertichi is an early mammal from Madagascar that lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 65-70 million years ago. This relatively large mammal, weighing around 10-12 kg, represents one of the few larger mammals known from the Mesozoic Era and provides valuable insights into mammalian diversity before the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

images.title: Cartorhynchus lenticarpus
images.description: Cartorhynchus lenticarpus is an early ichthyosaur from the Triassic period, representing one of the most basal known members of the ichthyosaur lineage. This small marine reptile possessed a distinctive cartilaginous snout and provides crucial insights into the early evolution of these successful ocean-dwelling predators.

images.title: Tanystropheus longobardicus
images.description: Tanystropheus longobardicus was a bizarre Triassic reptile characterized by an extraordinarily long neck that could exceed the length of its entire body, making it one of the most unusual protosaurs. This semi-aquatic creature likely used its elongated neck to hunt for fish and small prey in shallow marine environments.

images.title: Cosesaurus aviceps
images.description: Cosesaurus aviceps was a small, early archosaur from the Triassic period, notable for its bird-like skull features and semi-aquatic adaptations. This early member of Protorosauria represents an important transitional form in the evolution of archosaurs.

images.title: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
images.description: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus was a massive theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous North Africa, notable for being one of the largest carnivorous dinosaurs and possessing a distinctive sail-like structure on its back formed by elongated neural spines. Recent fossil evidence suggests it was highly aquatic, spending much of its time hunting in river and ocean environments.

images.title: Priosphenodon avelasi
images.description: Priosphenodon avelasi is an extinct sphenodontian from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina, representing a lineage of lizard-like reptiles that survived long after most of their relatives disappeared. These specialized herbivorous or omnivorous reptiles possessed robust jaws adapted for processing tough plant material.

images.title: Rhombodus binkhorsti
images.description: Rhombodus binkhorsti is an extinct chimaeroid fish from the Paleozoic era, characterized by its diamond-shaped tooth plates used for crushing hard-shelled prey. As a member of Chondrichthyes, it represents an early relative of modern chimaeras and ratfish.

images.title: Gephyrosaurus bridensis
images.description: Gephyrosaurus bridensis is an early sphenodont from the Jurassic period, representing one of the oldest known members of this lineage that survives today in tuataras. This small, lizard-like reptile inhabited Early Jurassic environments and provides important insights into the early evolution of sphenodontians.

images.title: Kaiwhekea katiki
images.description: Kaiwhekea katiki is an Early Jurassic plesiosaur from New Zealand, representing one of the earliest known members of Sauropterygia. This marine reptile exemplifies the diversity of Mesozoic marine ecosystems, with adaptations for aquatic predation in ancient ocean environments.

images.title: Hexanchus
images.description: Hexanchus is an ancient cow shark characterized by its distinctive six gill slits, a primitive feature among sharks that has persisted relatively unchanged for millions of years. This deep-sea predator represents an early lineage of sharks that thrived from the Jurassic period onward and continues to exist in modern oceans.

images.title: Aristonectes quiriquinensis
images.description: Aristonectes quiriquinensis was a large plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of South America, notable for its extremely long neck containing over 70 cervical vertebrae. As a member of the Sauropterygia, it was a marine reptile that hunted fish and other prey in ancient seas.

images.title: Sinosaurosphargis yunguiensis
images.description: Sinosaurosphargis yunguiensis is an early sauropterygian from the Middle Triassic of China, representing one of the most basal members of this marine reptile group. This small aquatic predator possessed flippers and a streamlined body adapted for hunting in ancient seas.

images.title: Pezosiren portelli
images.description: Pezosiren portelli is an early sirenian from the Eocene epoch that represents a transitional form between fully aquatic sea cows and their land-dwelling ancestors. This herbivorous marine mammal possessed hind limbs that were still somewhat functional, distinguishing it from later sirenians that lost their hind limbs entirely.

images.title: Seymouria baylorensis
images.description: Seymouria baylorensis was a small, lizard-like reptiliomorph from the Early Permian period that represents an important transitional form between amphibians and amniotes. This early synapsid predator inhabited freshwater environments and displayed characteristics intermediate between these two major vertebrate groups.

images.title: Diplocaulus magnicornis
images.description: Diplocaulus magnicornis was a small lepospondyl amphibian from the Permian period, characterized by its distinctive broad, boomerang-shaped head with lateral horn-like extensions. This aquatic predator used its flattened body and unusual cranial morphology to hunt small fish and invertebrates in freshwater environments.

images.title: Madygenerpeton pustulatus
images.description: Madygenerpeton pustulatus is an early reptiliomorph from the Carboniferous period, representing a transitional form between amphibians and true reptiles. This small creature exhibits characteristics that help paleontologists understand the early evolution of amniotes and the colonization of terrestrial environments.

images.title: Chroniosaurus dongusensis
images.description: Chroniosaurus dongusensis is an early synapsid from the Permian period of Russia, representing an early member of the therapsid lineage that eventually led to mammals. This small reptiliomorph inhabited the arid floodplains of the early Permian and displayed characteristics intermediate between pelycosaurs and more derived synapsids.

images.title: Zby atlanticus
images.description: Zby atlanticus is an early sauropodomorph from the Middle Triassic of Morocco, representing a transitional form in the evolution toward the giant sauropods of later periods. This relatively small dinosaur provides important insights into sauropodomorph origins and the early diversification of this group.

images.title: Hyperodapedon sanjuanensis
images.description: Hyperodapedon sanjuanensis was a herbivorous rhynchosaur from the Middle Triassic of Argentina, characterized by its distinctive beaked snout and specialized dental plates adapted for processing tough plant material. This relatively large member of the Rhynchosauria was part of the diverse reptilian fauna that dominated terrestrial ecosystems before the rise of dinosaurs.

images.title: Chiniquodon theotonicus
images.description: Chiniquodon theotonicus was a small carnivorous cynodont therapsid from the Early Triassic of South America, representing an advanced member of the lineage that would eventually lead to mammals. This agile predator possessed specialized teeth and likely hunted small reptiles and arthropods in the post-Permian extinction recovery ecosystems.

images.title: Ischigualastia jenseni
images.description: Ischigualastia jenseni was a large dicynodont therapsid from the Early Triassic of Argentina, representing one of the herbivorous synapsids that survived the Permian-Triassic extinction event. This tusked, barrel-bodied creature was among the dominant herbivores of its time before dinosaurs rose to prominence.

images.title: Palaeolyngbya barghoorniana
images.description: Palaeolyngbya barghoorniana is an ancient cyanobacterium (filamentous bacterium) from the Precambrian era, known from microfossil evidence in Archean and Proterozoic rocks. It represents some of the earliest evidence of oxygenic photosynthesis and was instrumental in the Great Oxidation Event that transformed Earth's atmosphere.

images.title: Chanaresuchus ischigualastensis
images.description: Chanaresuchus ischigualastensis was a small, crocodile-like protorosaur from the Early Triassic of Argentina. This early archosauromorph represents a transitional form in the evolution toward modern crocodilians and dinosaurs.

images.title: Saturnalia tupiniquim
images.description: Saturnalia tupiniquim is one of the earliest known sauropodomorphs from the Late Triassic of Brazil, representing a transitional form between smaller prosauropods and the giant sauropods that would dominate the Mesozoic. This small herbivorous dinosaur provides crucial insights into the early evolution of the sauropodomorph lineage.

images.title: Mei long
images.description: Mei long was a small theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous China, notable for being one of the first dinosaurs discovered in a sleeping posture with its head tucked under its arm. This crow-sized troodontid provides rare direct evidence of dinosaur resting behavior and sleep positions.

images.title: Lesothosaurus diagnosticus
images.description: Lesothosaurus diagnosticus was a small, early ornithischian dinosaur from Early Jurassic South Africa, representing one of the most basal members of the Genasauria clade. This agile herbivore possessed a bipedal stance and simple leaf-shaped teeth adapted for processing plant material.

images.title: Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis
images.description: Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis was a large carnivorous theropod dinosaur from Middle Jurassic China, reaching lengths of around 10-11 meters. This apex predator was characterized by a powerful build, sharp claws, and teeth adapted for hunting large herbivorous dinosaurs of its time.

images.title: Tyrannosaurus rex
images.description: Tyrannosaurus rex was a massive carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, characterized by its powerful jaws, sharp teeth, and bipedal stance. As one of the largest land predators ever discovered, it dominated its ecosystem as an apex predator.

images.title: Deinocheirus mirificus
images.description: Deinocheirus mirificus was a bizarre theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, renowned for its unusually long arms equipped with massive claws and an enigmatic body plan that remained poorly understood until recent fossil discoveries. This unusual predator represents one of paleontology's most distinctive theropod adaptations.

images.title: Therizinosaurus cheloniformis
images.description: Therizinosaurus cheloniformis was one of the largest known theropod dinosaurs, distinguished by its enormous curved claws on its forelimbs that could exceed 1 meter in length. Despite its fearsome appearance, this Late Cretaceous giant was likely an herbivorous or omnivorous theropod that used its massive claws for foraging and defense.

images.title: Supersaurus vivianae
images.description: Supersaurus vivianae was one of the largest land animals ever to exist, a colossal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Middle to Late Jurassic period. This long-necked herbivore could reach lengths of over 100 feet and weighed up to 50 tons, using its extremely elongated neck to browse vegetation from tall trees.

images.title: Tarbosaurus bataar
images.description: Tarbosaurus bataar was a large tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur from Late Cretaceous Mongolia, closely related to Tyrannosaurus rex. This apex predator reached lengths of up to 12 meters and hunted large herbivorous dinosaurs across the arid floodplains of ancient Asia.

images.title: Stygimoloch spinifer
images.description: Stygimoloch spinifer was a pachycephalosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, characterized by its distinctive thick, domed skull and prominent spikes protruding from the back of its head. This bipedal herbivore likely used its reinforced skull in intraspecific combat with other members of its species.

images.title: Homalocephale calathocercos
images.description: Homalocephale calathocercos was a small pachycephalosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, characterized by its relatively flat skull dome and small body size compared to other members of its family. This herbivorous dinosaur likely used its thickened skull in intraspecific combat and social displays within its herd communities.

images.title: Sinornithosaurus millenii
images.description: Sinornithosaurus millenii was a small feathered theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous China, representing an important transitional form between velociraptors and early birds. This dromaeosaur possessed both dinosaurian and avian characteristics, including feathers, a sickle claw, and a relatively long tail.

images.title: Sauroposeidon proteles
images.description: Sauroposeidon proteles was one of the largest land animals ever to exist, a massive sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period known for its extraordinarily long neck and towering height that could reach up to 60 meters. This herbivorous giant used its extreme height to browse vegetation from the tops of trees, dominating the landscape of North America during the Aptian age.

images.title: Mercuriceratops gemini
images.description: Mercuriceratops gemini was a small ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North America, characterized by paired brow horns and a distinctive frill. This early horned dinosaur represents an important transitional form in ceratopsian evolution.

images.title: Giraffatitan brancai
images.description: Giraffatitan brancai was one of the largest land animals ever to exist, a massive sauropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Africa that could reach lengths of over 30 meters. With its extremely long neck and columnar legs, this herbivore was specially adapted for feeding on high vegetation in its arid environment.

images.title: Achanarella trewini
images.description: Achanarella trewini is an early agnathan (jawless fish) from the Ordovician period, representing one of the earliest vertebrates with a distinct body structure. This small, armored fish exemplifies the diversity of early jawless fishes that dominated ancient aquatic environments before the rise of jawed vertebrates.

images.title: Qianzhousaurus sinensis
images.description: Qianzhousaurus sinensis was a mid-sized carnivorous theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous China, notable for its distinctive large nasal crest and relatively short arms. This agile predator represents an important transitional form in theropod evolution during the Early Cretaceous period.

images.title: Cornovichthys blaauweni
images.description: Cornovichthys blaauweni is an early jawless fish (agnathan) from the Paleozoic Era, characterized by its distinctive horn-like projections and primitive body structure. As a member of the Agnatha, it represents an important stage in early vertebrate evolution before the development of jaws.

images.title: Euphanerops longaevus
images.description: Euphanerops longaevus was an early jawless fish (agnathan) from the Devonian period, characterized by its elongated body and primitive fin structures. This ancient vertebrate represents an important step in fish evolution, bridging the gap between earlier jawless fish and more derived vertebrates.

images.title: Stylemys nebrascensis
images.description: Stylemys nebrascensis is an extinct terrestrial turtle from the Oligocene epoch of North America. This genus is notable for its relatively small size and adaptations to semi-arid environments of the Great Plains region.

images.title: Perchoerus probus
images.description: Perchoerus probus was an early omnivorous artiodactyl that lived during the Eocene epoch in North America. This small, pig-like mammal represents an early branch of the even-toed ungulates that would eventually diversify into pigs, peccaries, deer, and cetaceans.

images.title: Haikouichthys ercaicunensis
images.description: Haikouichthys ercaicunensis is an early agnathan fish from the Cambrian period, representing one of the earliest known vertebrates. This small, jawless fish possessed a notochord and primitive fins, making it crucial to understanding the evolution of vertebrate body plans.

images.title: Anzu wyliei
images.description: Anzu wyliei is a large oviraptorosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, known for its distinctive head crest and powerful forelimbs. This theropod was likely an omnivorous opportunistic feeder that inhabited floodplain environments.

images.title: Onchopristis numidus
images.description: Onchopristis numidus was a large sawfish-like ray from the Cretaceous period, characterized by its elongated snout armed with tooth-like rostral teeth used for slashing and detecting prey in ancient marine environments. This Early to Mid-Cretaceous predator inhabited shallow seas and estuaries across North Africa and the Mediterranean region.

images.title: Cotylocara macei
images.description: Cotylocara macei is an extinct early cetacean from the Eocene epoch, representing an intermediate stage in whale evolution with features bridging land mammals and fully aquatic whales. This small proto-whale inhabited shallow marine and coastal environments during the early diversification of cetaceans.

images.title: Semirostrum ceruttii
images.description: Semirostrum ceruttii is an extinct baleen whale from the Miocene epoch, representing an early stage in the evolution of modern baleen whales. This species possessed a partially developed rostrum and represents a transitional form between toothed and filter-feeding cetaceans.

images.title: Eromangasaurus australis
images.description: Eromangasaurus australis was a plesiosaur from Early Cretaceous Australia, belonging to the Sauropterygia group of marine reptiles. This four-flippered predator inhabited shallow seas and estuaries, hunting fish and other marine prey with its elongated body and powerful limbs.

images.title: Torvosaurus gurneyi
images.description: Torvosaurus gurneyi was a large carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period, known from fossils found in Portugal. This apex predator was one of the larger theropods of its time, measuring up to 10 meters in length and equipped with powerful claws and teeth for hunting.

images.title: Umoonasaurus demoscyllus
images.description: Umoonasaurus demoscyllus was a plesiosaur from the Early Cretaceous period that inhabited the ancient seas of Australia. This long-necked marine reptile was an apex predator that used its flexible neck and sharp teeth to hunt fish and other marine prey.

images.title: Platypterygius longmani
images.description: Platypterygius longmani was a medium-sized ichthyosaur from the Cretaceous period, characterized by its streamlined body and powerful tail flukes for efficient aquatic locomotion. This marine reptile was an apex predator that hunted fish and other marine organisms in Cretaceous seas.

images.title: Cryolophosaurus ellioti
images.description: Cryolophosaurus ellioti was an early theropod dinosaur from Early Jurassic Antarctica, notable for its distinctive V-shaped crest and relatively large size for its time. This apex predator inhabited a polar ecosystem and represents one of the earliest known large carnivorous dinosaurs.

images.title: Kronosaurus queenslandicus
images.description: Kronosaurus queenslandicus was a large plesiosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its powerful flippers, long neck, and formidable teeth adapted for hunting marine prey. As a member of the Sauropterygia, it dominated the shallow seas of what is now Queensland, Australia.

images.title: Charnia masoni
images.description: Charnia masoni is a frond-like organism from the Ediacaran period, characterized by its feather-shaped or leaf-like body plan with a central axis and lateral branches. It is one of the earliest known large complex organisms and likely represents a sessile filter feeder that lived on the seafloor.

images.title: Branisella boliviana
images.description: Branisella boliviana is one of the oldest known primates from South America, dating to the Oligocene epoch around 26-27 million years ago. This small primate is an important fossil for understanding early primate evolution and the dispersal of primates across the Americas.

images.title: Monolophosaurus jiangi
images.description: Monolophosaurus jiangi was a mid-sized theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China, characterized by a distinctive single crest running along its skull. This carnivorous dinosaur represents an early experiment in cranial ornamentation among theropods and provides insights into the diversity of predators during the Jurassic period.

images.title: Dunkleosteus terrelli
images.description: Dunkleosteus terrelli was a massive armored fish (placoderm) from the Late Devonian period, reaching lengths of up to 10 meters and possessing powerful blade-like jaws capable of crushing prey. As an apex predator of ancient seas, it dominated marine ecosystems during the height of the Age of Fishes.

images.title: Dilophosaurus wetherilli
images.description: Dilophosaurus wetherilli was an early theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its distinctive paired cranial crests and moderate size of approximately 20 feet in length. As one of the largest predators of its time, it represents an important transitional form in theropod evolution.

images.title: Gobivenator mongoliensis
images.description: Gobivenator mongoliensis is a small early cretaceous theropod dinosaur from Mongolia known for its primitive features and relatively simple skeletal structure. This early-diverging dromaeosaur represents an important transitional form in the evolution of small predatory dinosaurs.

images.title: Agujaceratops mariscalensis
images.description: Agujaceratops mariscalensis was a mid-sized ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico, characterized by its distinctive nasal horn and facial ornamentation typical of the ceratopsian family. This herbivorous dinosaur represents an important lineage in the evolution of horned dinosaurs in North America.

images.title: Atopodentatus unicus
images.description: Atopodentatus unicus was a bizarre marine reptile from the Middle Triassic with an unusual tooth-like structure in its upper jaw used for filter-feeding on small organisms. This sauropterygian represents one of the most unusual feeding strategies among Mesozoic marine reptiles.

images.title: Machairodus catocopis
images.description: Machairodus catocopis was a saber-toothed felid from the Miocene epoch, characterized by its elongated canine teeth adapted for hunting large prey. This powerful carnivore roamed Eurasian landscapes as one of the apex predators of its time.

images.title: Mosasaurus missouriensis
images.description: Mosasaurus missouriensis was a large marine reptile from the Late Cretaceous that dominated shallow seas across North America. This apex predator possessed powerful jaws, a flexible spine, and a paddle-like tail, making it one of the most formidable marine hunters of its time.

images.title: Omeisaurus tianfuensis
images.description: Omeisaurus tianfuensis was a medium-sized sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China, characterized by its relatively modest size compared to later giant sauropods. This herbivorous dinosaur represents an important transitional form in sauropod evolution during the Jurassic period.

images.title: Asylosaurus yalensis
images.description: Asylosaurus yalensis is an early sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic period, representing a transitional form between smaller prosauropods and the giant sauropods that would dominate later epochs. This herbivorous dinosaur exhibits characteristics that bridge the gap between bipedal and fully quadrupedal locomotion in sauropodomorph evolution.

images.title: Coryphodon eocaenus
images.description: Coryphodon eocaenus was a large, hippopotamus-like mammal from the early Eocene epoch, belonging to the order Cimolesta. This herbivorous creature possessed a robust build and was among the largest land mammals of its time.

images.title: Tylosaurus nepaeolicus
images.description: Tylosaurus nepaeolicus was a large marine mosasaur that dominated Late Cretaceous seas with its powerful jaws and streamlined body. As an apex predator, it hunted fish, smaller marine reptiles, and other large sea creatures in the Western Interior Seaway.

images.title: Stenopterygius quadriscissus
images.description: Stenopterygius quadriscissus was a small to medium-sized ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic, characterized by its streamlined body and four-cusped teeth adapted for catching small fish and squid. This marine reptile was a powerful swimmer that dominated Jurassic seas alongside other ichthyosaurs and plesiosaurs.

images.title: Megacerops coloradensis
images.description: Megacerops coloradensis was a large brontothere, a horned perissodactyl mammal from the Eocene epoch. This rhinoceros-like herbivore was characterized by a distinctive bony horn-like protuberance on its snout and robust build, representing one of the largest members of its family.

images.title: Teratophoneus curriei
images.description: Teratophoneus curriei was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid theropod from the Early Cretaceous of North America, measuring approximately 8 meters in length. This predator represents an intermediate form in tyrannosauroid evolution, predating the giant tyrannosaurs of the Late Cretaceous.

images.title: 2013 in Paleontology
images.description: A composite poster celebrating significant paleontological discoveries and notable extinct organisms from 2013, showcasing the diversity of life across different geological periods and environments.

images.title: Panthera blytheae
images.description: Panthera blytheae is an extinct leopard species from the Pliocene epoch of the Tibetan Plateau, representing one of the earliest known members of the Panthera genus. This ancient big cat lived in high-altitude environments and provides insight into the evolutionary history of modern leopards and lions.

images.title: Archicebus achilles
images.description: Archicebus achilles is one of the earliest known primates, dating back approximately 55 million years to the Eocene epoch. This small, tree-dwelling mammal represents a crucial early stage in primate evolution, with primitive features that bridge earlier mammalian ancestors and more modern primates.

images.title: Thalattoarchon saurophagis
images.description: Thalattoarchon saurophagis was a large apex predatory ichthyosaur from the Middle Triassic, measuring up to 8 meters in length and featuring a powerful bite adapted for hunting other marine reptiles. Its name means 'ruler of the sea' and 'lizard-eater,' reflecting its role as one of the ocean's dominant carnivores during its time.

images.title: Barbaturex morrisoni
images.description: Barbaturex morrisoni is an extinct varanid lizard from the Eocene epoch, notable for being one of the largest terrestrial squamates known from fossil records. This large monitor lizard inhabited tropical and subtropical environments during the early Cenozoic era.

images.title: Sulcavis geeorum
images.description: Sulcavis geeorum is an early enantiornithine bird from the Early Cretaceous of China, characterized by primitive skeletal features and preserved evidence of feather impressions. This small arboreal avialan represents an important transitional form in the evolution of modern birds.

images.title: Europelta carbonensis
images.description: Europelta carbonensis is an early ankylosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Spain, representing one of the oldest known members of the armored dinosaur clade Thyreophora. This small herbivore was protected by bony plates and osteoderms embedded in its skin, a defining characteristic of the thyreophoran lineage.

images.title: Obdurodon tharalkooschild
images.description: Obdurodon tharalkooschild is an extinct monotreme from Australia, representing an early member of the egg-laying mammal lineage that survived into the Miocene epoch. As a more derived relative of modern platypuses, it possessed venomous spurs and specialized adaptations for an aquatic lifestyle.

images.title: Eosinopteryx brevipenna
images.description: Eosinopteryx brevipenna was a small, feathered theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China, characterized by its short wings and transitional morphology between non-avian dinosaurs and early birds. This early-branching avian displays primitive features that provide insight into the evolution of flight and feather development in dinosaurs.

images.title: Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus
images.description: Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus was a large hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous of China, notable for its distinctive hollow cranial crest that protruded forward from its skull. This herbivorous ornithopod was one of the few crested hadrosaurs known from Asia and represents an important branch of duck-billed dinosaur evolution.

images.title: Edmontosaurus regalis
images.description: Edmontosaurus regalis was a large hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, characterized by its distinctive duck-like bill and complex dental batteries used for processing plant material. As one of the last non-avian dinosaurs, it was an abundant herbivore that lived in herds across coastal floodplains.

images.title: Xiphactinus audax
images.description: Xiphactinus audax was a large predatory fish from the Cretaceous period, reaching lengths of up to 4.5 meters. This ray-finned fish was one of the apex predators of ancient seas, equipped with sharp teeth and a powerful body adapted for hunting other fish.

images.title: Platecarpus tympaniticus
images.description: Platecarpus tympaniticus was a marine mosasaur, a large predatory lizard that dominated Cretaceous seas. This apex predator possessed powerful jaws, a flexible spine, and a paddle-like tail, making it an efficient hunter of fish and smaller marine reptiles.

images.title: Meniscoessus robustus
images.description: Meniscoessus robustus was a small, robust multituberculate mammal from the Late Cretaceous period. This early mammal possessed specialized teeth for processing tough plant material and represents an important branch of early mammalian evolution.

images.title: Kritosaurus navajovius
images.description: Kritosaurus navajovius was a large hadrosaur (duck-billed dinosaur) from the Late Cretaceous of North America, characterized by a distinctive arched nasal crest that may have played a role in species recognition or vocalization. As a member of Ornithopoda, it was a herbivorous dinosaur adapted for grazing on low vegetation in Late Cretaceous ecosystems.

images.title: Ichthyosaurs of the Upper Lias of England
images.description: The Upper Lias (Toarcian stage) of England was home to diverse ichthyosaur communities during the Early Jurassic. These marine reptiles were apex predators of the shallow seas that covered much of Britain, representing various genera and sizes that dominated the Mesozoic oceans.

images.title: Ichthyosaurs of the Lower Lias of England
images.description: The Lower Lias (Early Jurassic) seas of England were dominated by ichthyosaurs, a diverse group of marine reptiles that convergently evolved to resemble modern dolphins and sharks. These apex predators thrived in shallow epicontinental seas and left abundant fossils in the shale and limestone deposits of this period.

images.title: Hauffiopteryx typicus
images.description: Hauffiopteryx typicus was a relatively small ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its streamlined body and paddle-like flippers adapted for efficient marine locomotion. This member of the Ichthyosauria was an apex predator in Jurassic seas, hunting fish and other small marine creatures.

images.title: Stenopterygius triscissus
images.description: Stenopterygius triscissus was a relatively small ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its streamlined body and three-cusped teeth adapted for catching small fish and marine invertebrates. This genus is particularly well-known from exceptional fossil specimens that preserve details of skin, fin structure, and even embryos, providing invaluable insights into ichthyosaur reproduction and anatomy.

images.title: Ichthyosaurus communis
images.description: Ichthyosaurus communis was a relatively small ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, measuring around 2 meters in length. This marine reptile was a powerful swimmer with a streamlined body, large eyes adapted for deep diving, and needle-like teeth specialized for catching fish and squid.

images.title: Ichthyosaurus breviceps
images.description: Ichthyosaurus breviceps was a relatively small ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its notably short snout compared to other ichthyosaur species. As a marine reptile, it was a streamlined predator adapted for hunting fish and other small marine prey in Jurassic seas.

images.title: Eurhinosaurus longirostris
images.description: Eurhinosaurus longirostris was a long-snouted ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its distinctively elongated rostrum which it likely used to probe for small prey in marine environments. This marine reptile represents an adaptation to specialized feeding strategies within Mesozoic oceans.

images.title: Excalibosaurus costini
images.description: Excalibosaurus costini was a Early Jurassic ichthyosaur characterized by an elongated, sword-like rostrum that gave it its distinctive name. This marine reptile was an efficient predator adapted to life in Mesozoic oceans.

images.title: Leptonectes tenuirostris
images.description: Leptonectes tenuirostris was an early ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its slender, pointed snout adapted for catching small fish and marine prey. This relatively small marine reptile represents an early stage in ichthyosaur evolution before the group achieved its larger, more robust forms in later periods.

images.title: "Leptonectes" acutirostris
images.description: Leptonectes acutirostris was a small Early Jurassic ichthyosaur characterized by its elongated, pointed snout adapted for hunting small fish and marine prey. This early member of the ichthyosaurs represents a transitional form in the evolution of these highly successful marine reptiles.

images.title: Temnodontosaurus platyodon
images.description: Temnodontosaurus platyodon was a large marine ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its powerful jaws lined with sharp teeth and a streamlined body adapted for hunting fish and smaller marine reptiles. This apex predator could reach lengths of up to 10 meters and dominated the shallow seas of its time.

images.title: Crocs from the Purbeck Limestone, England
images.description: The Purbeck Limestone of England preserves a diverse assemblage of crocodylomorphs from the Early Cretaceous, representing various ecological roles in ancient freshwater and brackish environments. These extinct relatives of modern crocodilians ranged from small, agile hunters to larger apex predators that coexisted with early dinosaurs and other reptiles.

images.title: Bernissartia fagesii
images.description: Bernissartia fagesii was a small, early crocodylomorph from the Early Cretaceous of Belgium, measuring only about 60 centimeters in length. This primitive crocodile relative represents an important transitional form in crocodylomorph evolution during the Mesozoic Era.

images.title: Goniopholis simus
images.description: Goniopholis simus was a goniopholidid crocodylomorph that lived during the Cretaceous period, representing an early relative of modern crocodilians. This semi-aquatic predator inhabited freshwater environments and was characterized by its elongated snout and robust build adapted for hunting fish and small vertebrates.

images.title: Ajancingenia yanshini
images.description: Ajancingenia yanshini was a small troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, characterized by its bipedal posture, large brain relative to body size, and predatory adaptations. This feathered dinosaur represents the highly derived lineage of small, intelligent theropods that thrived in the Cretaceous period.

images.title: Lythronax argestes
images.description: Lythronax argestes was an early tyrannosaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Utah, representing one of the most primitive members of the tyranosaur family. This apex predator roamed semi-arid floodplain environments approximately 98 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.

images.title: Gallimimus bullatus
images.description: Gallimimus bullatus was a small to medium-sized omnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, known for its long legs, lightweight build, and ostrich-like appearance that made it one of the fastest dinosaurs. This agile runner likely fed on plants, insects, and small animals while relying on speed and agility to evade larger predators.

images.title: Struthiomimus altus
images.description: Struthiomimus altus was a small, bipedal omnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, known for its long legs, small head, and ostrich-like body adapted for swift running and foraging.

images.title: Deinocheirus mirificus
images.description: Deinocheirus mirificus was a bizarre theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous characterized by its enormous curved claws on its forelimbs, which were twice as long as its legs. This enigmatic predator's function and hunting behavior remained mysterious until more complete fossil specimens were discovered.

images.title: Koparion douglassi
images.description: Koparion douglassi was a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its diminutive size and specialized teeth adapted for consuming small prey. This rare dinosaur provides important insights into the diversity of early theropod lineages.

images.title: Geminiraptor suarezarum
images.description: Geminiraptor suarezarum was a small dromaeosaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous of North America, known from fossil remains discovered in Utah. This feathered predator was characterized by its paired sickle-shaped claws and likely hunted small prey in Early Cretaceous ecosystems.

images.title: Troodon inequalis
images.description: Troodon inequalis was a small, intelligent theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, known for its enlarged brain relative to body size and specialized sickle-shaped claw on each foot. This omnivorous troodontid was among the most cognitively advanced dinosaurs of its time.

images.title: Talos sampsoni
images.description: Talos sampsoni is a small theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, known from fossil remains discovered in Montana. This diminutive predator represents one of the smaller members of the theropod lineage.

images.title: North American Dromaeosauridae
images.description: A composite illustration of the diverse dromaeosaurid theropods that inhabited North America during the Cretaceous period. This group of small to medium-sized predators were characterized by their sickle-shaped claws, high intelligence, and pack hunting behaviors.

images.title: Yurgovuchia doellingi
images.description: Yurgovuchia doellingi is a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Russia, known from fragmentary remains including teeth and skeletal elements. This diminutive predator represents an early lineage of theropods that inhabited Early Cretaceous ecosystems.

images.title: Atrociraptor marshalli
images.description: Atrociraptor marshalli was a small dromaeosaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, measuring approximately 2 meters in length. This agile predator possessed the characteristic sickle-shaped claws and feathered body typical of raptorial dinosaurs.

images.title: Utahraptor ostrommaysorum
images.description: Utahraptor ostrommaysorum was one of the largest dromaeosaurs, reaching lengths of up to 7 meters, and lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Utah. This apex predator possessed a distinctive curved sickle claw on each foot and likely hunted in coordinated groups to take down large prey.

images.title: Saurornitholestes langstoni
images.description: Saurornitholestes langstoni was a small dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, known for its agility and grasping claws. This swift predator likely hunted small vertebrates and may have been an opportunistic scavenger in its ecosystem.

images.title: Dromaeosaurus albertensis
images.description: Dromaeosaurus albertensis was a small dromaeosaur theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, characterized by its relatively small size, grasping claws, and swift predatory adaptations. This early member of the dromaeosaur family represents the evolution of sophisticated hunting behaviors and collaborative pack hunting strategies in small theropod dinosaurs.

images.title: Platyhystrix rugosus
images.description: Platyhystrix rugosus was an early temnospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its robust build and textured skin. As a member of the Temnospondyli, it represents an important lineage of early tetrapods that dominated freshwater ecosystems before the rise of amniotes.

images.title: Eotyrannus lengi
images.description: Eotyrannus lengi was an early tyrannosauroid theropod from the Early Cretaceous period, representing one of the most primitive members of the tyrannosaur lineage. This relatively small predator demonstrates the evolutionary origins of the dominant carnivorous dinosaurs that would later dominate the Late Cretaceous.

images.title: Noasaurus leali
images.description: Noasaurus leali was a small theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina, known for its enlarged sickle-shaped claw on its second toe similar to dromaeosaurs. This agile predator represents an early divergence in the evolution of specialized hunting claws among theropod dinosaurs.

images.title: Basal Ceratosauria
images.description: Basal ceratosaurs represent the earliest members of the ceratosaur lineage, a group of theropod dinosaurs characterized by horns and crests on their skulls. These carnivorous dinosaurs ranged from the Early to Late Jurassic periods and were important predators in their respective ecosystems.

images.title: Bahariasaurus ingens
images.description: Bahariasaurus ingens was a massive theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North Africa, rivaling Tyrannosaurus in size and representing one of the apex predators of its time. This carnivorous dinosaur possessed powerful claws and teeth, making it a formidable hunter in its Saharan ecosystem.

images.title: Elaphrosaurus bambergi
images.description: Elaphrosaurus bambergi was a small to medium-sized theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period, characterized by its slender build, long neck, and carnivorous diet. This agile predator was one of the fastest dinosaurs of its time and inhabited the semi-arid floodplains of what is now Tanzania.

images.title: Berberosaurus liassicus
images.description: Berberosaurus liassicus was an early theropod dinosaur from North Africa during the Early Jurassic period, representing one of the oldest known members of the theropod lineage. This primitive carnivorous dinosaur provides important insights into the early evolution and diversification of theropod dinosaurs.

images.title: Megalosauridae
images.description: Megalosauridae was a family of large carnivorous theropod dinosaurs that dominated predator niches during the Early and Middle Jurassic periods. These bipedal hunters were characterized by powerful hind limbs, sharp claws, and robust skulls, making them apex predators of their time.

images.title: Leshansaurus qianweiensis
images.description: Leshansaurus qianweiensis was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China, known from fossils discovered in Sichuan Province. This bipedal predator represents part of the diverse theropod fauna that inhabited Early Cretaceous Asia.

images.title: Torvosaurus tanneri
images.description: Torvosaurus tanneri was a large carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period, characterized by powerful jaws, sharp teeth, and a robust build suited for hunting large herbivorous dinosaurs. It was one of the apex predators of its time, rivaling Allosaurus in size and predatory role.

images.title: Magnosaurus nethercombensis
images.description: Magnosaurus nethercombensis was a mid-sized theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of England, known from fossils discovered in the Wealden Formation. This carnivorous dinosaur represents an important part of the Early Cretaceous European theropod fauna.

images.title: Oviraptor philoceratops
images.description: Oviraptor philoceratops was a small theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, characterized by its distinctive crested head, toothless beak, and feathered body. Despite its name meaning "egg thief," it was likely an omnivorous scavenger that fed on small animals, plants, and eggs.

images.title: Aralosaurus tuberiferus
images.description: Aralosaurus tuberiferus was a mid-sized ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Central Asia, characterized by its herbivorous adaptations and relatively primitive iguanodontian features. This genus represents an important transitional form in ornithopod evolution during the early stages of their diversification.

images.title: Rugosodon eurasiaticus
images.description: Rugosodon eurasiaticus was a small Early Cretaceous mammal from what is now Mongolia, characterized by its specialized dental features adapted for grinding tough plant material. As a member of the early mammalian fauna, it represents the diverse but diminutive mammals that coexisted with dinosaurs during the Mesozoic Era.

images.title: Psittacosaurus lujiatunensis
images.description: Psittacosaurus lujiatunensis is an early ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China, known for its parrot-like beak and small herbivorous body plan. This primitive member of the Ceratopsia shows early evolutionary steps toward the larger horned dinosaurs that would dominate later periods.

images.title: Ocepechelon bouyai
images.description: Ocepechelon bouyai was an unusual sea turtle from the Late Cretaceous period, notable for its disproportionately large head relative to its body size. This bizarre adaptation may have housed expanded sensory organs or feeding apparatus specialized for a unique ecological niche in ancient marine ecosystems.

images.title: Megaconus mammaliaformis
images.description: Megaconus mammaliaformis was a small, furry mammaliaform from the Jurassic period that possessed unique cone-shaped teeth adapted for insectivory. This early relative of true mammals represents an important transitional form in the evolution of Mesozoic mammal-like creatures.

images.title: Velociraptor mongoliensis
images.description: Velociraptor mongoliensis was a small, bipedal theropod dinosaur from Mongolia known for its intelligence, pack hunting behavior, and distinctive curved claw on each foot. This agile predator inhabited the arid floodplains and deserts of the Early Cretaceous period.

images.title: Melanerpeton tenerum
images.description: Melanerpeton tenerum was a small, early temnospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its delicate build and aquatic adaptations. This primitive tetrapod represents an important transitional form in the evolution of early amphibians.

images.title: Pantelosaurus saxonicus
images.description: Pantelosaurus saxonicus was a small pelycosaur from the Early Permian of Saxony, Germany, representing an early member of the synapsid lineage that would eventually lead to mammals. This primitive carnivorous synapsid inhabited the warm, humid forests of the early Permian period.

images.title: Tangasaurus mennelli
images.description: Tangasaurus mennelli is an early synapsid from the Permian period of Tanzania, representing an early member of the Younginiformes group. This small, lizard-like creature represents an important transitional form in the evolution of synapsids toward more derived groups.

images.title: Thadeosaurus colcanapi
images.description: Thadeosaurus colcanapi was an early amniote from the Carboniferous period, representing one of the early members of Younginiformes. This small, lizard-like reptile was among the earliest vertebrates to develop an amniotic egg, allowing it to reproduce away from water.

images.title: Youngina capensis
images.description: Youngina capensis was a small, agile reptile from the Early Permian of South Africa, measuring around 60 centimeters in length. It is considered one of the earliest members of Younginiformes, an important basal group in early amniote evolution that bridged primitive synapsids and later diapsid reptiles.

images.title: Corosaurus alcovensis
images.description: Corosaurus alcovensis was a small marine reptile belonging to the sauropterygians, a diverse group of aquatic predators that dominated ancient seas. This species inhabited the shallow seas of North America during the Jurassic period, using its flexible body and paddle-like limbs to hunt fish and other small prey.

images.title: Pliosaurus kevani
images.description: Pliosaurus kevani was a large marine reptile belonging to the pliosaurids, a group of apex predators that dominated Jurassic and Cretaceous oceans. These powerful swimmers possessed four flippers, a streamlined body, and formidable jaws equipped with sharp teeth for hunting large marine prey.

images.title: Acrotholus audeti
images.description: Acrotholus audeti was a small pachycephalosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, characterized by its distinctive thick, domed skull used for intraspecific combat. This bipedal herbivorous dinosaur represents one of the earliest known members of the pachycephalosaur family.

images.title: Albertadromeus syntarsus
images.description: Albertadromeus syntarsus was a small herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, measuring only about 1.3 meters in length. It represents one of the smallest known ornithopods and is characterized by its fused ankle bones (syntarsus), which gave it enhanced agility for evading predators.

images.title: Archaeopteryx lithographica
images.description: Archaeopteryx lithographica is a transitional fossil from the Late Jurassic period that exhibits both theropod dinosaur and avian characteristics, including feathers, wings, and a long bony tail. It is considered one of the earliest known birds and provides crucial evidence for the evolutionary link between dinosaurs and modern birds.

images.title: Alamosaurus sanjuanensis
images.description: Alamosaurus sanjuanensis was one of the last and largest sauropods, reaching lengths of up to 35 meters and weighing nearly 70 tons. This titanosaur inhabited North America during the Late Cretaceous Period, representing a lineage that survived until the end-Cretaceous mass extinction.

images.title: Judiceratops tigris
images.description: Judiceratops tigris is an early ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China, representing a transitional form between basal ceratopsians and more derived horned dinosaurs. This small herbivore possessed early developments of the cranial features that would become prominent in later ceratopsians.

images.title: Bravoceratops polyphemus
images.description: Bravoceratops polyphemus was a small ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, characterized by its distinctive cranial ornamentation and single brow horn. This herbivorous dinosaur represents an early member of the horned dinosaur lineage that would later diversify into the iconic ceratopsids of the Late Cretaceous.

images.title: Aurornis xui
images.description: Aurornis xui is an early avian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of China, representing one of the oldest known bird-like dinosaurs with well-preserved feather impressions. This small predator bridges the gap between non-avian theropods and modern birds, exhibiting both primitive and advanced characteristics.

images.title: Turiasaurus riodevensis
images.description: Turiasaurus riodevensis was one of the largest sauropods ever discovered, a massive long-necked herbivorous dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Spain. This titanosaur could reach lengths of up to 40 meters and weighed as much as 80 tons, making it among the most enormous land animals to have ever existed.

images.title: Zarafasaura oceanis
images.description: Zarafasaura oceanis was a medium-sized plesiosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North Africa, characterized by its long neck and streamlined body adapted for marine predation. This sauropterygian was an active swimmer that hunted fish and other small marine organisms in ancient ocean environments.

images.title: Elanodactylus prolatus
images.description: Elanodactylus prolatus was a pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its elongated wings and specialized adaptations for aerial locomotion. This flying reptile was part of the diverse pterosaur fauna that dominated Mesozoic skies.

images.title: Concornis lacustris
images.description: Concornis lacustris was an early bird from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its small size and primitive features that bridge non-avian dinosaurs and modern birds. This fossil bird inhabited freshwater lake environments in what is now Spain.

images.title: Pelecanimimus polydon
images.description: Pelecanimimus polydon was a small theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Spain, notable for being one of the most basal ornithomimosaurs with an unusually high tooth count for its group. It represents an important transitional form in theropod evolution.

images.title: Iberomesornis romerali
images.description: Iberomesornis romerali was an early bird from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain, representing an intermediate stage in avian evolution between Archaeopteryx and modern birds. This small theropod possessed both primitive and derived features, including teeth, clawed wings, and a partially fused skeleton.

images.title: Diandongosaurus acutidentatus
images.description: Diandongosaurus acutidentatus was a small Early Triassic sauropterygian reptile from China, characterized by its sharp, pointed teeth adapted for catching small aquatic prey. As an early member of the Sauropterygia, it represents the transitional forms between terrestrial reptiles and the marine reptiles that would dominate Mesozoic oceans.

images.title: Dianopachysaurus dingi
images.description: Dianopachysaurus dingi was a small nothosaur from the Middle Triassic period, representing an early stage in the evolution of marine reptiles. This carnivorous sauropterygian hunted fish and smaller prey in Triassic seas using its streamlined body and powerful tail.

images.title: Aragosaurus ischiaticus
images.description: Aragosaurus ischiaticus was a large sauropodomorph dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Spain, representing one of the earliest known sauropods of the Iberian Peninsula. This long-necked herbivore inhabited arid fluvial environments during the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Cretaceous period.

images.title: Tastavinsaurus sanzi
images.description: Tastavinsaurus sanzi was a Early Cretaceous sauropodomorph dinosaur from North Africa, representing one of the earliest known macronarian sauropods. This long-necked herbivore inhabited semi-arid floodplain environments during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous period.

images.title: Lirainosaurus astibae
images.description: Lirainosaurus astibae was a small sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Spain, representing one of the last surviving members of the sauropod lineage in Europe. This relatively diminutive sauropod inhabited the Iberian Peninsula during a time when most sauropods had already disappeared from other continents.

images.title: Arenysaurus ardevoli
images.description: Arenysaurus ardevoli was a small ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Spain, characterized by its bipedal locomotion and herbivorous diet. This early member of the Ornithopoda represents the diverse small dinosaurian fauna that inhabited European ecosystems during the Cretaceous period.

images.title: Pararhabdodon isonensis
images.description: Pararhabdodon isonensis was a small ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Spain, characterized by its leaf-shaped teeth and bipedal locomotion. This herbivorous dinosaur was part of the diverse fauna that inhabited Iberian environments during the Barremian stage.

images.title: Dinosaurs of Niger
images.description: Niger's dinosaur fauna represents a rich Early Cretaceous ecosystem that thrived in what was once a lush, river-dominated landscape. This diverse assemblage included iconic theropods, sauropods, and other Gondwanan fauna that dominated the African continent during the Aptian to Albian stages.

images.title: Irhazer Group
images.description: The Irhazer Group is a Middle Jurassic fossil assemblage from Niger that preserves a diverse fauna including sauropods, theropods, and early crocodyliforms in a fluvial to lacustrine environment. This ecosystem represents a critical window into Gondwanan dinosaur communities during the Middle Jurassic period.

images.title: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis
images.description: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis was a mid-sized sauropodomorph from the Middle Jurassic of Niger, characterized by distinctive spines running along its vertebral column. This herbivorous dinosaur represents an important transitional form in sauropod evolution.

images.title: Spinostropheus gautieri
images.description: Spinostropheus gautieri was a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Africa, characterized by its slender build and bipedal locomotion typical of early carnivorous dinosaurs. This genus represents an important member of early theropod evolution during the Cretaceous.

images.title: Afrovenator abakensis
images.description: Afrovenator abakensis was a mid-sized theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Africa, measuring approximately 8-9 meters in length. This carnosaurian predator represents an important example of theropod diversity in the ancient African continent during the Aptian-Albian ages.

images.title: Jobaria tiguidensis
images.description: Jobaria tiguidensis was a long-necked sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Niger, representing one of the few sauropods known from Africa during this period. This massive herbivore reached lengths of up to 18 meters and possessed the characteristic columnar legs and elongated neck typical of sauropod dinosaurs.

images.title: Elrhaz Formation
images.description: The Elrhaz Formation is a Early Cretaceous geological formation located in Niger, Africa, known for its diverse assemblage of dinosaurs and other fauna from approximately 121-125 million years ago. This ecosystem represents a fluvial (river-based) environment that preserved numerous theropod, sauropod, and ornithischian dinosaurs alongside crocodilians and other vertebrates.

images.title: Eocarcharia dinops
images.description: Eocarcharia dinops was an early theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Africa, known for its distinctive large forward-facing eyes that gave it enhanced binocular vision. This 8-9 meter long predator was one of the earliest members of the carcharodontosaur group, apex predators that would later dominate Cretaceous ecosystems.

images.title: Nigersaurus taqueti
images.description: Nigersaurus taqueti was a long-necked sauropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Africa, notable for its unusually short neck compared to other sauropods and its specialized peg-like teeth adapted for feeding on low-growing vegetation. This 9-meter-long herbivore represents an unique adaptation among sauropodomorphs for grazing on ferns and cycads near ground level.

images.title: Elrhazosaurus nigeriensis
images.description: Elrhazosaurus nigeriensis was an early iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Niger, representing one of the earliest known members of the Iguanodontia clade. This herbivorous dinosaur was a medium-sized bipedal dinosaur with adaptations for processing tough plant material.

images.title: Ouranosaurus nigeriensis
images.description: Ouranosaurus nigeriensis was a large herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Africa, notable for possessing a distinctive sail-like structure formed by elongated neural spines along its back. This bipedal dinosaur inhabited the warm, semi-arid environments of what is now Niger during the Aptian stage.

images.title: Suchomimus tenerensis
images.description: Suchomimus tenerensis was a large spinosaurid theropod from Early Cretaceous Niger, characterized by its crocodile-like snout, prominent dorsal sail, and semi-aquatic lifestyle. This piscivorous dinosaur was well-adapted for hunting fish and other aquatic prey in river and lake environments.

images.title: Kryptops palaios
images.description: Kryptops palaios is an Early Cretaceous theropod dinosaur known for its unusual facial features, including a distinctive crest and mysteriously reduced eye sockets. This predator represents an interesting lineage of abelisaurid theropods that dominated southern landmasses during the Cretaceous period.

images.title: Lurdusaurus arenatus
images.description: Lurdusaurus arenatus was a mid-sized ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Africa, characterized by its bipedal locomotion and herbivorous diet. This genus represents an important transitional form in ornithopod evolution, displaying features intermediate between earlier and later members of the group.

images.title: Echkar Formation Fauna
images.description: Reconstruction of the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage, ~95 Ma) fauna of the Echkar Formation in Niger, portraying large theropods such as Carcharodontosaurus and Spinosaurus alongside titanosaurs in a lush floodplain environment.

images.title: Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis
images.description: Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis was a massive carnivorous theropod dinosaur from North Africa, belonging to the carcharodontosaur family of apex predators. This early Cretaceous giant was among the largest terrestrial carnivores ever to exist, rivaling Tyrannosaurus rex in size and dominance.

images.title: Rugops primus
images.description: Rugops primus was an early theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of North Africa, notable for being one of the most basal known members of the Spinosauridae family. This unusual predator possessed a distinctive rough, bumpy skull texture and is thought to have been a semi-aquatic hunter adapted to riverside and floodplain environments.

images.title: Dinosaurs of New Jersey
images.description: New Jersey during the Mesozoic Era was home to a diverse array of dinosaurs, including theropods, sauropods, and ornithischians that inhabited the coastal lowlands and floodplains of the eastern North American seaway. This composite artwork depicts the rich paleofauna that inhabited the region during the Cretaceous Period.

images.title: Hadrosaurus foulkii
images.description: Hadrosaurus foulkii was an early hadrosaur (duck-billed dinosaur) from the Late Cretaceous period of North America. As one of the first dinosaurs to be scientifically named, it was a herbivorous ornithopod that used its specialized dental batteries to process tough plant material.

images.title: Dryptosaurus aquilunguis
images.description: Dryptosaurus aquilunguis was a large theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America, closely related to Tyrannosaurus and characterized by sharp, serrated teeth adapted for slicing through flesh. This apex predator was an active hunter that dominated its coastal and fluvial ecosystems during the Maastrichtian stage.

images.title: Heterodontosaurus tucki
images.description: Heterodontosaurus tucki was a small Early Jurassic ornithischian dinosaur known for its distinctive heterodont dentition—teeth of different shapes and sizes adapted for varied diets. This bipedal herbivore was one of the most basal members of Heterodontosauria and provides important insights into early ornithischian evolution.

images.title: Camarillas formation
images.description: The Camarillas Formation is a Early Cretaceous geological unit from Spain that preserves a diverse assemblage of dinosaurs and other fauna from the Lower Cretaceous period. This ecosystem represents a fluvial depositional environment with various theropod and sauropod dinosaurs coexisting in a semi-arid to temperate climate.

images.title: Camarillasaurus cirugedae
images.description: Camarillasaurus cirugedae was a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Spain. This bipedal carnivore represents the diverse fauna of Early Cretaceous Iberia.

images.title: Delapparentia turolensis
images.description: Delapparentia turolensis was a small ornithopod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous Spain, characterized by its bipedal locomotion and herbivorous diet. This primitive member of the Ornithopoda was well-adapted to the varied terrain of Iberia during the Barremian age.

images.title: British Dinosaurs
images.description: This composite illustration depicts various dinosaur species that inhabited the British Isles during the Mesozoic Era, showcasing the diverse fauna that roamed these regions during different time periods. The image represents an important part of paleontological history, as Britain has yielded significant dinosaur fossil discoveries including iguanodontids, theropods, and sauropods.

images.title: Megalosaurus bucklandii
images.description: Megalosaurus bucklandii was one of the first dinosaurs formally named and described, representing a large carnivorous theropod from the Middle Jurassic period. This apex predator possessed powerful hind limbs, sharp claws, and a robust build that made it a dominant hunter in its Early to Middle Jurassic ecosystems.

images.title: Polacanthus foxii
images.description: Polacanthus foxii was a small to medium-sized ankylosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England, distinguished by its array of bony plates and spikes running along its back and sides for defense. As a member of the Thyreophora, it was an armored herbivorous dinosaur adapted to browsing low vegetation.

images.title: Scelidosaurus harrisonii
images.description: Scelidosaurus harrisonii was an early armored dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period, featuring bony osteoderms embedded in its skin for protection. As one of the earliest known members of Thyreophora, it represents a transitional form between unarmored and heavily plated dinosaurs.

images.title: Baryonyx walkeri
images.description: Baryonyx walkeri was a large spinosaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous period, known for its distinctive crocodile-like skull, prominent sail-like dorsal spines, and powerful claws on its forelimbs. This semi-aquatic predator was one of the largest carnivorous dinosaurs of its time and likely hunted fish and other prey both in water and on land.

images.title: Eotyrannus lengi
images.description: Eotyrannus lengi was an early tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, representing one of the most primitive members of the tyrannosaur lineage. This relatively small predator exhibits characteristics intermediate between earlier non-tyrannosauroid theropods and the giant tyrannosaurids of the Late Cretaceous.

images.title: Hypsilophodon foxii
images.description: Hypsilophodon foxii was a small, bipedal herbivorous dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its lightweight build, long tail for balance, and relatively small size compared to other ornithopods. This agile creature was an early member of the Ornithopoda clade and likely relied on speed and maneuverability to evade predators.

images.title: Iguanodon bernissartensis
images.description: Iguanodon bernissartensis was a large herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, notable for its distinctive thumb spikes and bipedal locomotion. This species is one of the most well-known iguanodonts, with numerous fossil specimens discovered in the Bernissart formation of Belgium providing detailed knowledge of its anatomy and behavior.

images.title: Vectocleidus pastorum
images.description: Vectocleidus pastorum was a small plesiosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, belonging to the sauropterygian group of marine reptiles. This long-necked marine predator inhabited shallow coastal seas and fed on fish and other small marine organisms.

images.title: Yulong mini
images.description: Yulong mini was a small theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China, notable for being one of the smallest known members of its lineage. This diminutive predator represents the diversity of small carnivorous dinosaurs that coexisted during the Cretaceous period.

images.title: Trinisaura santamartaensis
images.description: Trinisaura santamartaensis was a small ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Colombia, representing one of the earliest known ornithopods from South America. This bipedal herbivore possessed the characteristic features of early ornithopods, including specialized teeth for processing plant material.

images.title: Europasaurus holgeri
images.description: Europasaurus holgeri was a dwarf sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Germany, notable for being one of the smallest known sauropods at approximately 6-9 meters in length. This herbivorous dinosaur likely represents a case of island dwarfism, adapted to the limited resources of the European archipelago during the Wealden period.

images.title: Enaliornis barretti
images.description: Enaliornis barretti was an early toothed bird from the Early Cretaceous period, representing a transitional form between non-avian dinosaurs and modern birds. This small aquatic or semi-aquatic bird possessed primitive features such as teeth and a bony tail, alongside developing avian characteristics.
