This small, lizard-like creature inhabited freshwater environments and possessed adaptations for semi-aquatic life, including a flattened tail for swimming.

images.title: Seymouria baylorensis
images.description: Seymouria baylorensis was a small, lizard-like reptiliomorph from the Early Permian period, representing a transitional form between amphibians and amniotes. This early synapsid was an important link in understanding the evolution of terrestrial vertebrates during the Paleozoic Era.

images.title: Stenopterygius quadriscissus
images.description: Stenopterygius quadriscissus was a relatively small ichthyosaur from the Early Jurassic period, characterized by its streamlined body and four flipper-like limbs adapted for rapid aquatic locomotion. This marine reptile was a formidable predator of ancient seas, feeding on fish and smaller marine organisms.

images.title: Cymbospondylus petrinus
images.description: Cymbospondylus petrinus was a large marine reptile belonging to the ichthyosaurs, a diverse group of dolphin-like predators that dominated the oceans during the Mesozoic Era. This species inhabited Triassic seas and possessed a streamlined body, powerful tail, and sharp teeth adapted for hunting fish and other marine prey.

images.title: Procolophon trigoniceps
images.description: Procolophon trigoniceps was a small, lizard-like reptile from the Early Triassic period, characterized by its distinctive triangular skull and robust build. This early procolophonomorph was an early synapsid survivor of the Permian-Triassic extinction event.

images.title: Bauria cynops
images.description: Bauria cynops was a small carnivorous therapsid from the Triassic period, characterized by its single opening in the temporal region of its skull and relatively advanced mammal-like features. This predatory synapsid represents a transitional form in the evolution toward true mammals.

images.title: Panderichthys rhombolepis
images.description: Panderichthys rhombolepis was a lobe-finned fish from the Late Devonian period that represents an important transitional form between fish and tetrapods. This freshwater predator possessed robust fins, a flattened body, and a primitive neck region, exhibiting characteristics that bridge aquatic and terrestrial vertebrate evolution.

images.title: Hovasaurus boulei
images.description: Hovasaurus boulei was a small, lizard-like eosuchian reptile from the Permian period of Madagascar. It represents an early member of the sauropsid lineage and provides important insights into the early evolution of reptiles.

images.title: Milleretta rubidgei
images.description: Milleretta rubidgei was a small parareptile from the Permian period, characterized by its lizard-like body and primitive reptilian features. This early amniote represents an important branch in reptilian evolution, distinct from the more successful synapsids and sauropsids of its time.

images.title: Gorgosaurus libratus
images.description: Gorgosaurus libratus was a medium-sized tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur that inhabited North America during the Late Cretaceous period. This apex predator reached lengths of up to 8-9 meters and was known for its powerful bite and agile hunting capabilities.

images.title: Kannemeyeria simocephalus
images.description: Kannemeyeria simocephalus was a large dicynodont therapsid from the Triassic period, characterized by its robust build and distinctive paired tusks protruding from its upper jaw. This herbivorous synapsid was one of the most successful large mammals of its time, roaming the semi-arid floodplains of what is now South Africa.

images.title: Varanops brevirostris
images.description: Varanops brevirostris was a small carnivorous pelycosaur from the Early Permian period, characterized by its short snout and sharp teeth adapted for hunting small prey. As an early synapsid, it represents a transitional form in the evolutionary lineage leading toward mammals.

images.title: Inostrancevia alexandri
images.description: Inostrancevia alexandri was a large carnivorous therapsid from the Permian period, notable for its saber-like canine teeth and powerful predatory build. As one of the apex predators of its time, it dominated terrestrial ecosystems before the great Permian-Triassic extinction event.

images.title: Othnielosaurus consors
images.description: Othnielosaurus consors was a small herbivorous theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period, characterized by its bipedal stance and lightweight frame adapted for swift movement. This dinosaur represents an early lineage of ornithopods that thrived during the Lower Cretaceous of North America.

images.title: Proburnetia viatkensis
images.description: Proburnetia viatkensis was a small carnivorous therapsid from the Permian period, characterized by its robust build and powerful jaws adapted for hunting small prey. This early synapsid represents an important transitional form in the evolutionary lineage toward mammals.

images.title: Edaphosaurus pogonias
images.description: Edaphosaurus pogonias was a large herbivorous pelycosaur from the Carboniferous period, characterized by a distinctive sail-like structure on its back formed by elongated neural spines. This synapsid was one of the early amniotes and represents an important lineage in the evolution toward modern mammals.

images.title: Anteosaurus magnificus
images.description: Anteosaurus magnificus was a large carnivorous therapsid from the Permian period, representing one of the apex predators of its time with powerful jaws and robust build. As a saber-toothed synapsid, it dominated terrestrial ecosystems before the rise of dinosaurs.

images.title: Diplocaulus magnicornis
images.description: Diplocaulus magnicornis was a distinctive amphibian from the Permian period, characterized by its unusual boomerang-shaped head with laterally extended horns. This semi-aquatic creature likely used its distinctive skull shape for hydrodynamic purposes or intraspecific signaling in freshwater environments.

images.title: Eogyrinus attheyi
images.description: Eogyrinus attheyi was an early reptiliomorph from the Carboniferous period, representing a transitional form between amphibians and amniotes. This small, lizard-like creature possessed characteristics of both groups and inhabited the swampy forests of early tetrapod evolution.

images.title: Jonkeria truculenta
images.description: Jonkeria truculenta was a large carnivorous therapsid from the Permian period, characterized by its robust build and powerful jaws adapted for hunting other synapsids. This machairodontan-like predator represents the apex carnivores of the mid-Permian fauna of South Africa.

images.title: Haptodus garnettensis
images.description: Haptodus garnettensis was an early synapsid from the Carboniferous period, belonging to the pelycosaurs, a group of proto-mammals that dominated terrestrial ecosystems before the rise of dinosaurs. This small carnivorous predator possessed sharp teeth and a streamlined body adapted for hunting smaller vertebrates in ancient swamps and forests.

images.title: Estemmenosuchus mirabilis
images.description: Estemmenosuchus mirabilis was a large, herbivorous synapsid from the Early Permian of Russia, characterized by distinctive bony protrusions on its skull and a robust build adapted for browsing vegetation. This early therapsid represents an important stage in the evolution of synapsids toward more mammal-like forms.

images.title: Biarmosuchus tener
images.description: Biarmosuchus tener was an early therapsid from the Permian period, representing one of the basal members of the group that would eventually lead to mammals. This small predator possessed distinctive paired temporal openings and teeth specialized for gripping prey.

images.title: Titanophoneus potens
images.description: Titanophoneus potens was a large carnivorous therapsid from the Permian period, representing one of the apex predators of its time before the rise of dinosaurs. This powerful synapsid was characterized by its robust build and formidable teeth, making it a dominant predator in early amniote ecosystems.

images.title: Eothyris parkeri
images.description: Eothyris parkeri is an early pelycosaur from the Carboniferous period, representing one of the earliest synapsids and ancestors of mammals. This small, lizard-like predator exhibits the primitive characteristics of early amniotes and played an important ecological role in early terrestrial ecosystems.

images.title: Diadectes sideropelicus
images.description: Diadectes sideropelicus was a large, herbivorous reptiliomorph from the Carboniferous period, representing one of the earliest known tetrapods to adopt a plant-based diet. This stocky, quadrupedal creature possessed powerful jaws adapted for processing tough vegetation and could reach lengths of up to 3 meters.

images.title: Osteolepis macrolepidotus
images.description: Osteolepis macrolepidotus was a lobe-finned fish (sarcopterygian) from the Middle Devonian period, characterized by its distinctive large, thick cosmoid scales and robust body structure. As an early representative of the group that would eventually give rise to tetrapods, it inhabited freshwater environments and played an important role in early vertebrate evolution.

images.title: Crassigyrinus scoticus
images.description: Crassigyrinus scoticus was an early tetrapod from Scotland that lived during the Carboniferous period, representing a transitional form between fish and fully terrestrial vertebrates. This aquatic or semi-aquatic creature possessed a robust body and powerful tail, adapted for hunting in freshwater environments of the Paleozoic era.

images.title: Tiktaalik roseae
images.description: Tiktaalik roseae is a transitional fossil between fish and tetrapods that lived during the Late Devonian period approximately 375 million years ago. This sarcopterygian possessed both fish-like features such as scales and fins, and tetrapod-like characteristics including a neck, robust limbs, and a flattened head, making it a crucial link in vertebrate evolution.

images.title: Ichthyostega stensioei
images.description: Ichthyostega stensioei is an early tetrapod from the Late Devonian period, representing a crucial transitional form between fish and four-legged vertebrates. This pioneering amphibian possessed both fish-like features such as a tail fin and gill structures, along with developing limbs adapted for movement in shallow aquatic environments.

images.title: Acanthostega gunnari
images.description: Acanthostega gunnari was an early tetrapod from the Late Devonian period, representing a crucial transitional form between fish and land-dwelling vertebrates. This limbed aquatic creature retained many fish-like features while possessing the eight-fingered limbs characteristic of early tetrapods.

images.title: Gogonasus andrewsae
images.description: Gogonasus andrewsae was a large lobe-finned fish from the Late Devonian period, notable for its advanced tetrapod-like features including limb-like fins and a mobile neck. This transitional form provides crucial evidence for the evolution of tetrapods from aquatic sarcopterygian ancestors.

images.title: Cotylorhynchus romeri
images.description: Cotylorhynchus romeri was a large herbivorous pelycosaur from the Early Permian period, characterized by its massive barrel-shaped body and relatively short limbs. This synapsid represents one of the apex herbivores of its time, though it would eventually be outcompeted by more derived synapsids.

images.title: Mesosaurus tenuidens
images.description: Mesosaurus tenuidens was an early parareptile from the Permian period, representing one of the earliest known amniotes adapted to a fully aquatic lifestyle. This small reptile possessed elongated jaws and a flattened tail, making it well-suited for hunting fish and other aquatic prey in ancient freshwater environments.

images.title: Eryops megacephalus
images.description: Eryops megacephalus was a large temnospondyl amphibian from the Early Permian period, characterized by its massive head and robust build. This apex predator of its time inhabited freshwater environments and is considered one of the most formidable amphibians of the Paleozoic era.

images.title: Archegosaurus decheni
images.description: Archegosaurus decheni was an early temnospondyl amphibian from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its large head and aquatic lifestyle. As a basal member of the Temnospondyli, it represents an important step in the evolution of tetrapods and their adaptation to freshwater environments.

images.title: Orthacanthus senckenbergianus
images.description: Orthacanthus senckenbergianus was a freshwater shark from the Carboniferous period, characterized by its elongated body, venomous dorsal spine, and tooth-bearing sail on its head. This apex predator inhabited Paleozoic freshwater ecosystems and represents an early diversification of cartilaginous fishes.

images.title: Metriorhynchus superciliosus
images.description: Metriorhynchus superciliosus was a marine crocodylomorph from the Jurassic period, adapted for life in ancient seas with a streamlined body and paddle-like limbs. These sleek predators were among the dominant reptilian carnivores of shallow marine ecosystems.

images.title: Pelagosaurus typus
images.description: Pelagosaurus typus was an early marine crocodylomorph from the Jurassic period, adapted for life in open ocean waters with a streamlined body and paddle-like limbs. This genus represents one of the earliest known pelagic crocodilians, distinct from its freshwater relatives.

images.title: Dimetrodon limbatus
images.description: Dimetrodon limbatus was a large carnivorous synapsid from the early Permian period, characterized by its distinctive tall sail-like dorsal fin supported by elongated neural spines. As a pelycosaur, it was among the dominant predators of its time and represents an early evolutionary branch leading toward mammals.

images.title: Sphenacodon ferox
images.description: Sphenacodon ferox was a carnivorous synapsid from the early Permian period, characterized by a sail-like structure on its back formed by elongated neural spines. As a member of the Pelycosauria, it was one of the dominant predators of its time before the rise of the therapsids.

images.title: Ophiacodon retroversus
images.description: Ophiacodon retroversus was a carnivorous pelycosaur from the early Permian period, characterized by its elongated body and powerful jaws adapted for hunting smaller vertebrates. As a basal synapsid, it represents an important transitional form in the evolutionary lineage leading to mammals.

images.title: Rugops primus
images.description: Rugops primus was an early theropod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous North Africa, known for its distinctive wrinkled facial features and relatively small size compared to later large carnivores. It represents one of the first apex predators to evolve in African ecosystems during the Cretaceous Period.

images.title: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis
images.description: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis was an early theropod dinosaur from the Late Triassic period, representing one of the earliest known large carnivorous dinosaurs. This bipedal predator possessed sharp claws and teeth, making it a formidable hunter in its ecosystem.

images.title: Lagosuchus talampayensis
images.description: Lagosuchus talampayensis was a small, bipedal dinosauromorph from the Middle Triassic of Argentina, representing an early relative of dinosaurs. This agile predator possessed a long tail for balance and is considered one of the closest non-dinosaurian relatives to the dinosaur lineage.

images.title: Lotosaurus adentus
images.description: Lotosaurus adentus was an early rauisuchian from the Middle Triassic period, representing one of the apex predators of its time with a powerful build and robust skull. As a member of Rauisuchia, it was part of a diverse group of semi-aquatic to terrestrial crocodile-like archosaurs that dominated many ecosystems before the rise of dinosaurs.

images.title: Macrauchenia patagonica
images.description: Macrauchenia patagonica was a large, camel-like ungulate from South America that lived during the Pleistocene epoch. This meridiungulate possessed an elongated body, long neck, and distinctive three-toed feet, representing one of the last survivors of a unique lineage that dominated the southern continents before the megafaunal extinctions.

images.title: Tuojiangosaurus multispinus
images.description: Tuojiangosaurus multispinus was a mid-sized stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China, characterized by its distinctive double rows of plates along the spine and multiple tail spikes for defense. As a member of Thyreophora, it represents the armored dinosaurs that dominated herbivorous niches during the Mesozoic Era.
